name: Mount Abu
description: Mount Abu is Rajasthan's only hill station, sitting at around 1,220 metres in the Aravalli Range near the Gujarat border. It suits families, honeymooners, and anyone needing relief from the desert heat, though the town itself is crowded and commercialised; the surrounding forests and temples reward those willing to walk a little. Not ideal for hardcore adventure travellers or those seeking isolation.
nearest_railhead: Abu Road (28 km from Mount Abu town)

attractions.name: Dilwara Jain Temples
attractions.description: A complex of five Jain temples built between the 11th and 13th centuries, renowned for extraordinarily intricate marble carvings on ceilings, pillars, and domes. The craftsmanship is genuinely world-class; the Vimal Vasahi and Luna Vasahi temples are the highlights.

attractions.name: Nakki Lake
attractions.description: A small natural lake at the centre of Mount Abu town, popular for paddle-boating and evening walks along its promenade. The surrounding rocky hills and Toad Rock nearby add some visual interest, though the waterfront itself gets crowded and commercial on weekends.

attractions.name: Guru Shikhar
attractions.description: The highest peak in the Aravalli Range at 1,722 metres, with a small Dattatreya temple at the summit and sweeping views across Rajasthan and Gujarat on clear days. The road goes almost to the top so it is accessible, but the last stretch involves stairs.

attractions.name: Achalgarh Fort
attractions.description: A 14th-century fort built by Rana Kumbha, now largely in ruins but still containing the Achaleshwar Mahadev temple with its unusual Shiva lingam. The site also has three large black buffalo statues and the Mandakini kund tank, making it an interesting cultural stop away from town crowds.

attractions.name: Sunset Point
attractions.description: A well-signposted viewpoint west of Nakki Lake offering views of the sunset over the Aravalli plains. It is extremely popular and gets genuinely crowded by late afternoon; the viewpoint itself is unremarkable but the sunset colours over the hills can be attractive.

attractions.name: Mount Abu Wildlife Sanctuary
attractions.description: A 290 sq km sanctuary covering the hills around Mount Abu, home to leopards, sloth bears, sambhar, and over 250 bird species including the grey jungle fowl. Leopard sightings are uncommon but possible; the Trevor's Tank area and forest trails around Nakki Lake offer good birding.

attractions.name: Brahma Kumaris World Spiritual University & Peace Park
attractions.description: Headquarters of the Brahma Kumaris organisation, with a large meditation centre, a museum explaining their philosophy, and a well-maintained Peace Park open to visitors. Whether or not you share the philosophy, the campus is calm and the views from the park are decent.

attractions.name: Trevor's Tank
attractions.description: A small reservoir built by a British engineer in the late 19th century, now a quiet crocodile habitat and reliable birding spot on the southern edge of the wildlife sanctuary. Few tourists make it here, making it one of the more peaceful corners of Mount Abu.

attractions.name: Adhar Devi Temple
attractions.description: A Durga temple carved into a natural rock cleft about 3 km north of town, reached by climbing 365 uneven stone steps through the hillside. It sees far fewer tourists than Dilwara and the views from the top over the surrounding forest are genuinely rewarding.
